draft.title: Wiradjuri resistance at Bathurst
card: The Wiradjuri are the Aboriginal people of a large part of central-western New South Wales. Their Country includes the land around Bathurst.
From 1815, colonists settled on Wiradjuri land around Bathurst. Their sheep and cattle used the water and grass that Wiradjuri people relied on for food.
The Wiradjuri resisted. Windradyne, a Wiradjuri man, led them in attacks on colonists' farms and stock in the early 1820s.
In 1824, Governor Brisbane declared martial law around Bathurst. This meant the army could use force under military rule instead of the usual courts. Many Wiradjuri people were killed.
draft.remember: Colonists took Wiradjuri land, Windradyne led resistance, and martial law in 1824 brought military force.

a.q: Why did the Wiradjuri resist the colonists around Bathurst?
opts: Colonists took their land, water and food sources
Colonists asked them to leave the region for good
Colonists blocked trade routes between Wiradjuri groups
Colonists banned them from holding ceremonies
a.why: The colonists' sheep and cattle used the water and grass the Wiradjuri relied on, and the settlers took over their Country. The other options describe things the card does not say happened.
a.clue: Think about what the colonists' farms and animals used.

b.q: In 1824 the governor declared martial law around Bathurst. What did this mean for the Wiradjuri?
opts: The army could use force without the usual courts
The Wiradjuri were given back their land
Colonists were told to stop farming near Bathurst
Windradyne was made a magistrate for the area
b.why: Martial law is military rule, so soldiers could use force instead of the usual courts. It did not return land or stop settlement. It was a response to the resistance, and many Wiradjuri were killed.
b.clue: Martial law means military rule in place of the usual courts.

a.q: Why did the Wiradjuri resist the colonists around Bathurst?
opts: Colonists took their land, water and food sources
Colonists asked them to leave the region for good
Colonists blocked trade routes between Wiradjuri groups
Colonists banned them from holding ceremonies
a.why: The colonists settled on Wiradjuri Country, and their sheep and cattle used the water and grass the Wiradjuri relied on for food. The colonists did not simply ask them to leave: they took the land and its resources, which is what the Wiradjuri resisted.
a.clue: Think about what the colonists' farms and animals used.

b.q: In 1824 the governor declared martial law around Bathurst. What did this mean for the Wiradjuri?
opts: The army could use force without the usual courts
Wiradjuri people could take disputes to the courts
Soldiers were sent away from the Bathurst district
Colonists were told to stop farming near Bathurst
b.why: Martial law put the area under military rule, so soldiers could use force instead of the usual courts. It did not send soldiers away or stop settlement. It was a response to Wiradjuri resistance, and many Wiradjuri were killed.
b.clue: Think about what the word martial refers to.
